why: The statement asks for Hausdorff and Minkowski dimension n for every n, so any single dimension is a case. Wang-Zahl 2025 settles n = 3 for both parts. I count it as digested: Guth, a named expert, published three digested rewrites of the proof, including a detailed outline of the reduction step and a Bourbaki survey. That is the kind of digestion F9 says counts, even though Guth says the survey does not sketch every step. The streamlined 2026 re-proof is the same result by the same authors, so it is unreviewed. The OpenAI 4D paper claims the Hausdorff part at n = 4, plus the Minkowski part for bounded sets. That is a case, unreviewed and doubtful because of its batch history and its dependency on an unreviewed lemma. No specific error has been found, so it is not knocked down. I score its AI role as generated: the paper has no human author, and the release README attributes the results to the model; the per-paper attribution comes only from where the paper sits in the release. The 3D maximal companion, Rios-Sawyer, the AlphaEvolve finite-field, arithmetic and planar results, and Borges et al. answer changed questions (variant). Borges et al.'s maximal estimate at 3.054 does not raise the general set bound above Katz-Zahl's 3.059. Rai Choudhuri's sticky R^4 result bounds a subclass; I scored it as a bound.
doubts: openai-math-074 bundles the same two manuscripts as openai-4d-2026-10 and openai-3d-maximal-2026-10; it is a duplicate, and I scored it like the 4D event. The AI attribution for the OpenAI papers rests on the release-wide README sentence, not on anything said about these papers. Hua-Yang's 'conditional repair' of the streamlined 3D reduction is unexplained; if it reveals a gap, the n = 3 verification would weaken. Verification for the older pre-snapshot bounds (Wolff, Katz-Laba-Tao, Katz-Tao) is inferred from long acceptance; their sources were not opened. Calling Wang-Zahl 2025 digested on the strength of Guth's expository work is a close call; the alternative is unreviewed, which would not change its tier.
